name: When was it completed?
question: The year each landmark was finished or opened.

items.name: Westminster Hall
items.fact: Westminster Hall is the oldest part of the Houses of Parliament.

items.name: Angkor Wat
items.fact: Angkor Wat is the largest religious structure in the world.

items.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
items.fact: Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire.

items.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
items.fact: Construction of the tower took almost 200 years.

items.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
items.fact: The current Golden Pavilion is a 1955 rebuild after an arson attack.

items.name: Forbidden City
items.fact: The Forbidden City has around 9,000 rooms, by legend 9,999.

items.name: Machu Picchu
items.fact: Machu Picchu was built without mortar.

items.name: Château de Chambord
items.fact: Its double-helix staircase may have been designed by Leonardo da Vinci.

items.name: St. Peter's Basilica
items.fact: Michelangelo designed St. Peter's dome.

items.name: Taj Mahal
items.fact: About 20,000 workers built the Taj Mahal.

items.name: St Paul's Cathedral
items.fact: St Paul's survived the Blitz almost untouched.

items.name: Big Ben (Elizabeth Tower)
items.fact: Big Ben's bell cracked shortly after it first rang.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge
items.fact: P. T. Barnum walked 21 elephants across the Brooklyn Bridge to prove it was safe.

items.name: Eiffel Tower
items.fact: The Eiffel Tower was meant to stand for only 20 years.

items.name: Panama Canal
items.fact: Ships are lifted 26 m above sea level to cross Panama.

items.name: Empire State Building
items.fact: The Empire State Building took just 410 days to build.

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge
items.fact: The bridge's color is called International Orange.

items.name: Sydney Opera House
items.fact: The Opera House opened ten years late and over budget.

items.name: CN Tower
items.fact: The CN Tower is hit by lightning about 75 times a year.

items.name: Burj Khalifa
items.fact: The Burj Khalifa has 163 floors.
